source: វិទ្យាការទប់ស្កាត់ និងកម្ចាត់សមាសភាពបទព្រុងលើដំណាំទុរេន (Prevention and Control of Harmful Organisms on Durian), Cambodian technical extension document compiled with reference to CABI Crop Protection Compendium and durian pest/disease literature, 28pp
text: Durian seed borer (Mudaria luteileprosa Holloway) is a moth pest whose larvae bore specifically toward the seed and surrounding flesh inside the fruit, often causing damage that is not visible from the outside of the husk until the fruit is opened, which makes it a difficult pest to detect and a serious quality-control problem for growers selling fruit by external appearance alone. General control approach described in the source: because external inspection alone is unreliable, growers in areas with known seed borer pressure are advised to periodically cut open a small sample of fruit near harvest time to check for internal damage before committing a full harvest batch to market, alongside routine insecticide timing recommended for the fruit-borer group of pests generally.
